research/experiment-protocol.md section 5: rate comparisons same box/same day/same code; quality comparison confounded only when a run is >10% short on steps; section 1 item 5: NEURON_CC_FLAGS must contain --optlevel=1 (controls use exactly '--optlevel=1')
expected_effect: Full 1800 s run: steps completed +3% to +8% vs same-host control (about 2135-2245 vs 2071 trn21 / 2076 trn22); public_val_bpb lower than the same-host control by 0.001 to 0.004 (predicted 1.002-1.005). Falsified if steps are within +/-1% of control (inert) or if bpb is not lower with >= +1% more steps. Predeclared: the smoke must already show >= +1.5% steps (>= 340 vs 334/335) or the hypothesis is discarded before the full run.
hypothesis: At the 9a4caa7b default shape the hashed n-gram value-embedding tables (ngram_ve True, tables=4 rows=1048576 dim=128, ~537M of the 592.9M parameters) receive a dense BF16 RMSprop update every step (opt=rmsprop flat_lr=True bf16=True rms_fp32_state_math=False nki_rms=False in both pinned control rows). The ngram-rms-fp32 smoke at this commit showed that changing only the arithmetic of that update moved step throughput by -5.7% (316 vs 335 steps in 300 s), so the table optimizer is on the step critical path and is plausibly HBM-bandwidth bound. Hypothesis: routing that update through the existing inline NKI kernel (--nki-ngram-rms) reduces the number of memory passes over the tables, raising steps completed in the fixed 1800 s budget by 3-8% with the same BF16 update semantics, and the extra steps translate to a lower public_val_bpb. This is a throughput-mediated quality hypothesis; numerical equivalence of the kernel path is itself a hypothesis to be checked by the smoke BPB gate, not an established fact.
single_causal_change: Pass --nki-ngram-rms only. Every other option stays at the 9a4caa7b defaults used by the two pinned controls: identical launch shape (NEURON_LOGICAL_NC_CONFIG=2, torchrun --nproc_per_node=4, --num-steps 5000, --max-train-seconds 1800, --seed 42), identical environment (NEURON_CC_FLAGS exactly '--optlevel=1', NEURON_COMPETITION_R1_SEED=42, PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1), no other kernel flag (no --nki-local-conv, --nki-attn, --nki-muon, --nki-relu2, --nki-rope-norm, --nki-softcap-ce), no precision flag (no --ngram-rms-fp32, --bf16-norm-output, --bf16-sdpa-input), no optimizer/schedule/batch/architecture/evaluation change. The only behavioral delta is the n-gram table RMSprop update executing via the NKI kernel path (nki_rms True in the resolved ngram_ve oneliner). Comparison: same-host pinned control on public_val_bpb (trn21 -> 2071 steps / 1.005734; trn22 -> 2076 steps / 1.005967). Outcome classes, mutually exclusive, evaluated in order: (1) CONFOUNDED-SHORT if candidate steps < 90% of same-host control steps (experiment-protocol.md section 5 rule; record as throughput regression only); (2) FALSIFIED-INERT if steps within +/-1% of control (kernel path is not faster or not reached); (3) EXCESS-GAIN-REVIEW if steps > +10% of control: record the throughput result and the BPB, but require a matched-step sanity check before any quality claim (a separately declared conservative upper rule, not the protocol's short-step rule); (4) SUCCESS if steps >= +1.5% and public_val_bpb < same-host control; (5) FALSIFIED-QUALITY if steps >= +1% and public_val_bpb >= same-host control (extra steps did not translate, or kernel numerics differ unfavorably); (6) INCONCLUSIVE if step gain is between +1% and +1.5%.
